A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ZeroTuning and retain matching core experiments. The main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results in Tables 1–3, token/layer/head experiments, and appendix robustness evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds unsupervised-calibration results, entropy analyses and confidence-dependent error evaluations.

M1.justification: v2 adds an unsupervised variant that selects heads and scaling factors by minimizing average next-token entropy on unlabeled test inputs (Section 3.6). v1 uses accuracy-based calibration and explicitly identifies dependence on ground truth as a limitation. The supervised rescaling procedure remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 15 benchmarks covering classification, multiple-choice QA and MT-Bench conversation. The context-extension, few-shot and prompt-variation scenarios are retained. New entropy and error analyses reuse existing datasets without extending task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding benchmark comparisons retain Vanilla, ACT and Auto-PASTA, with ACT restricted to Llama-3.1-8B using eager attention. Table 3 also retains the same conversation reference models. The new supervised/unsupervised comparison evaluates ZeroTuning variants.

E3.justification: v2 introduces evaluation with calibration on unlabeled test inputs, plus entropy sweeps and confidence-stratified error testing. Appendix B also specifies 500 calibration samples for all methods, replacing v1's ACT-specific 10% validation description. This is a reported protocol revision; unchanged benchmark scores do not establish that ACT was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of entropy–accuracy relationships, correction rates by initial confidence, extreme-tuning failures and misleading sample-level entropy minima (Appendices D–E). Appendix F expands the earlier output examples into paired Vanilla/ZeroTuning cases. Most existing ablations and robustness experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed 42 and report results without repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's new predictive-entropy and confidence analyses characterize model outputs rather than statistical uncertainty in benchmark estimates.

E6.justification: v2 Table 4 newly reports an unsupervised five-dataset average of 67.02, alongside 67.52 for supervised tuning and 59.00 for Vanilla. Entropy/confidence curves and expanded output cases add further findings. Tables 1–3 and the matched robustness tables retain their numerical results; larger headline percentages express relative improvements.

T1.justification: v2 formalizes tuning-effect magnitude and adds Proposition 1 with a derivative proof of its dependence on initial attention (Section 3.1 and Appendix C). It extends output-stability and temperature/argmax reasoning while dropping v1's value-state-drain premise. The core attention-rescaling and key-scaling derivations remain.

C1.justification: v2 makes unsupervised entropy-based calibration a central contribution and elevates reduced uncertainty and unlocking pretrained knowledge into main claims. Its abstract newly claims monotonic control of downstream attention entropy. The earlier claims about training-free, head-specific tuning and broad benchmark benefits are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive boundaries: entropy minimization can reinforce formatting errors or biased answers, and confident semantic errors resist correction while some confident formatting errors remain correctable. It expands explanations of extreme tuning and representation collapse. v1's explicit caveat about untested long-form reasoning is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 adds a LlamaAttention implementation snippet in Figure 1 and code/runnable-demo access information in the abstract. Framework, prompt and default hyperparameter disclosures are largely retained or relocated to Appendix B; this is a limited reproducibility-information expansion.

R1.justification: Citation changes include adding Han et al. (2025a,b) and removing LoRA+, several prompt-tuning works and some value-state references. The central positioning relative to PASTA, Auto-PASTA, ACT and attention-sink research remains substantially the same; detailed related work is relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and analysis narrative are extensively rewritten. A related-work summary moves near the beginning, detailed related work and experimental setup move into appendices, and the appendix sequence is reorganized around theory, failure analysis and unsupervised tuning.

P2.justification: v2 adds an implementation/heatmap overview, an attention schematic, entropy and error-analysis graphics, and an unsupervised-results table. It relocates the original scaling illustration to Appendix C and reformats tables, including correcting Table 1's duplicated SST-2 header to SST5. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 Appendix I leaves label dependence unresolved; v2 addresses it with a tested entropy-only variant achieving 67.02 versus 67.52 for supervised calibration on five datasets. The expanded failure and error analyses also substantially improve understanding of when tuning helps. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses, including an abstract entropy-control claim not established by the pairwise-difference proof and removal of the earlier long-form-reasoning caveat.
